svg.text: WARRANT on paper: the print register
GREYSCALE SHEET · AS A MONO LASER PRINTS IT (CIE Y)
A specimen for the operator’s judgement. A proposal: nothing on this sheet is approved, served or applied. Every number is read from a record named below it.
1 · THE FOUR STANDINGS: A LINE, AND A VALUE IN TEXT
float, or a number someone printed; nothing decided it
one member of a set the data admits
the edge a test adds to close an open file
no mark — the void is drawn
no certified exp. Weibull: choice refused
2 · THE VOID, THE WITNESS ×, THE GUIDE, THE MOOD
∅ and words, never a zero or a gap.
Buoy A, annual maxima: no certified fit for exp. Weibull.
exactly, it is 91. The one red, only on the × beside words.
certs/gsm8k-ledger.json: a counterexample shown, not deduced.
The guide, 2 3: a ruler, a ghost, a leader. It says nothing.
The monthly pick is lognormal given A²: a verdict that holds
given a chosen input names it, in italic. At that block KS picks
exp. Weibull; A², χ² and MSE pick lognormal (certs/hseva-ledger.json).
3 · THE REGISTER: VALUE, CONTRAST ON WHITE, ROLE
The order ramp: neutral, darker with magnitude, every step ΔL ≥ 0.06; black text reads on every step.
Identity, at most three series: ● ink, ■ the print blue (proposed), ▲ ink-3, each with its own marker.
Validator: design/print/REPORT.md, PASS: 9 of 9 checks, 13 of 13 red controls refused; every pair under protan, deutan, tritan.
4 · A DESIGN-WAVE FIGURE, REDRAWN: BUOY A, THE CERTIFIED 100-YEAR WAVE BY BLOCK
exp. Weibull, the block’s A² pick
hollow: the same family where A² picks the other
every marker decided: an enclosure narrower than the dot
a datum read from the record: decided
∅ refused: no mark, the void and words
NDBC hourly Hs, 175,320 hours over 22 years, pinned by sha256
hours and block maxima as independent draws from one law
maximum likelihood, no added location: a choice
picked by A² on the same sample; its tail is not tested
the record’s climate held, unchanged, for 100 years
The arithmetic is exact; the weakest premise is assumed, and so is every one.
Grades from /reports/hseva.html §3 (WARRANT v2.1); none was checked against the sea.
Buoy A (NDBC, the benchmark’s dataset A): the certified 100-year significant wave height of the two families Anderson–Darling picks somewhere on this buoy, by the block
the maxima are taken over. The block alone moves the picked level from 13.05 m (monthly, lognormal) to 17.38 m (weekly, exp. Weibull), a factor of 1.33.
Source: certs/hseva-ledger.json (generated 2026-10-21): fits, return levels, rankings, delta intervals, the aggregation finding.
5 · AN ENVIRONMENTAL-CONTOUR FIGURE, REDRAWN: DATASET A, THREE 20-YEAR CONTOURS OVER THE HOURS
expected outside by construction: 1 (total class, exact) · 11.5 (IFORM, enclosed)
an edge the file never listed: chosen
exact counts in chosen 0.25 s × 0.2 m cells: a drawing; 23 cells reach the top class
the hours: NDBC’s, 82,805 provided + 92,515 retained, pinned by sha256
the contours: each file’s literal vertices, pinned at the benchmark’s commit a1561fe7
the test: even-odd on the closed path (matplotlib’s convention), decided exactly;
the winding rule agrees on every hour (0 disagreements)
no × here: nobody claimed a count these files miss; a printed count that
differs would be a scalar that differs, not a witness (/instruments/contours)
Dataset A of the environmental-contour benchmark (Haselsteiner et al. 2021), 175,320 hours: three of the submitted 20-year contours drawn as their files list them, over
the hours they were scored on. The printed counts (the organizers’ float64 test: computed) reproduce exactly for all three.
Source: certs/ecbench-ledger.json (generated 2026-10-28); corpus/ec-benchmark datasets/A.txt + datasets-retained/Ar.txt and the three contour files, each checked against its sha256 pin here.
design/print/specimen.js · the register: design/print/tokens.js · the validator: design/print/REPORT.md · the stroke patterns: design/grammar.js, unchanged · MIT
Checked by design/print/check-svg.js before printing: only the five permitted dashes, only the register’s colours (here, their greys).
